correctness.rationale: For each unit direction \(\theta\), the radial restriction \(\phi_\theta(r)=f(x_*+r\theta)\) satisfies \(\phi_\theta'(r)\ge ar\). Hence its shell contribution is at most \(\delta/a\). If the angular integral attains \(2\pi\delta/a\), the nonnegative directional deficits vanish almost everywhere. Thus \(\phi_\theta'(r)=ar\) across the shell. The remainder \(h_\theta=\phi_\theta-f(x_*)-ar^2/2\) is convex with \(h_\theta'(0)=0\); vanishing of its derivative later forces it to vanish from the center to the outer shell. The outer radius is therefore the common value \(\sqrt{2(c+\delta-f(x_*))/a}\). Continuity of the radial function of the convex domain and continuity of \(f\) upgrade the almost-everywhere conclusion to the whole disk. The converse is the exact annulus-area calculation together with nonnegativity of the convex remainder.

value.rationale: The source emphasizes sharpness of a new exact planar constant but gives only an extremizing model. Classifying equality is the natural structural completion: it shows that one exact shell already forces the entire enclosed geometry and phase, rather than merely identifying another example. The conclusion is scale-invariant in form, rules out all nonquadratic finite-scale extremizers, and clarifies the rigidity hidden inside the radial proof.
